blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-security-1 (Bearer tokens are logged at info level with every request) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-security-2 (API tokens are stored in clear in the database) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
To diagnose integration problems, the middleware logs each request's
method, path and headers at `info` level, including `Authorization`, so
support can see which token an integration sent.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Every request is logged with its headers
findings.recommendation: Never log credentials (CWE-532). Anyone with read access to the logs (support, a log aggregator, a leaked log file) copies a valid bearer token from any request and calls the API as that user; since revocation is a Non-Goal, the stolen token stays valid indefinitely. The same decision also logs the `Cookie` header, exposing the session cookies `authenticate` reads in `src/http/middleware.rs`. Redact `Authorization` and `Cookie` (and any other credential header) before logging; to let support identify the token, log a non-secret token id or a short prefix instead. Update task 1.3 so `logs_requests` asserts the redaction.
findings.title: Bearer tokens are logged at info level with every request

findings.evidence:
The `api_tokens` table holds `user_id`, `token` and `created_at`; the
middleware looks a request's token up with `WHERE token = $1`. Storing the
token as given keeps the lookup a simple indexed equality.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Tokens are stored as given
findings.recommendation: Store a hash of the token, not the token (CWE-312 / CWE-256). Anyone who reads the `api_tokens` table — a database backup, a read-only replica, an SQL injection elsewhere — gets every user's working credential and can call the API as them, with no revocation to stop it. Since the tokens are 32 random bytes, a fast SHA-256 of the token is enough: store `token_hash` with a unique index and look up `WHERE token_hash = $1` on the hash of the presented token, which keeps the lookup a simple indexed equality. This also matches the spec's "shown once": the plaintext then exists only in the creation response. Update the migration of task 1.1 accordingly.
findings.title: API tokens are stored in clear in the database
